title: Multiplexed Nanoparticle Protein Corona Enables Accurate and Precise Deep Plasma Proteomics
projectDescription: The Proteograph Product Suite, a multiplexed nanoparticle (NP) protein corona-based proteomics workflow, substantially improves the depth of detection of proteins by mass spectrometry (MS) by compressing the dynamic range of protein abundances. Here, we explore the quantitative performance of the Proteograph Product Suite and its applicability to large-scale studies.  Using multi-species spike-in experiments, we investigated fold-change accuracy, linearity, precision and the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ) for the Proteograph Product Suite in conjunction with multiple MS instruments. We also manufactured four distinct lots of NPs (each capable of supporting over 100,000 assays) and evaluated batch to batch reproducibility.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Bovine plasma (K2EDTA, Innovative Research) was spiked into various human plasma samples for the accuracy study using multiple human backgrounds. Human samples included PC11 (a pooled plasma from 44 healthy donors), PC8 and PC9 (pooled from 4 and 5 donors, respectively), and four individual samples (SIA-D2, SIA-D8, SIA-H4, SIA-H7), all collected in K2EDTA and purchased from BioIVT.  Each spiked sample was processed using either the automated Proteograph workflow (XT Assay Kit V1.2) or a Neat plasma workflow. In Proteograph runs, peptides from NP-corona samples were eluted and dried via SpeedVac. For Neat workflow, digestion was performed directly on spiked plasma without NP incubation. Dried peptides were stored at –80°C and reconstituted in 0.1% FA and 3% ACN for DIA LC-MS analysis using Exploris 480 instruments (ThermoFisher Scientific).
dataProcessingProtocol: DIA-MS data were processed using DIA-NN v1.8.1 in library-free mode, searching against a combined Human and Bovine UniProt database (April 2022, 105,533 entries) without matching between runs. A 1% FDR threshold was applied at both precursor and protein levels. Precursor intensities were log₂-transformed, median-normalized within each spike-in ratio, and aggregated to protein intensities using the MaxLFQ method (via the R package "iq"). Only proteotypic (species-unique) peptides were used for quantification. Mixed peptides matching both human and bovine sequences were excluded. Accuracy evaluations were performed solely on bovine proteins, using bovine-unique peptides to estimate protein intensities and calculate log₂ fold changes.
